You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: HEAD responses served through http.ServeContent (or with no Content-Length) get a strong ETag computed from the empty body.

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] 304 drops `Last-Modified`. Criterion 4 says the 304 keeps "other headers"; only Content-Type, Content-Length and Content-Encoding are to be dropped. `writeNotModified` in etag.go does `h.Del("Last-Modified")` and etag_test.go:244 locks that in. Repro: handler sets `Last-Modified` and `Cache-Control`, request has `If-None-Match: *`. Result: `status=304 LM="" CC="max-age=60"`.
- [blocking] Wrapper changes handler-visible Write results. With handler `Content-Length: 3` and `Write("hello")`, plain net/http returns `n=0 err="http: wrote more than the declared Content-Length"`; through ETag it returns `n=5 err=<nil>`. The wire body matched in both cases, so this is a return-value difference, not a body one.
- [blocking] Hijack side effect. A handler that hijacks and writes a raw response (no buffered writes) makes `finish()` call `WriteHeader` on the hijacked connection, so net/http logs `http: response.WriteHeader on hijacked connection from ...startStreaming (etag.go:91)` on every hijacked GET. Plain net/http logs nothing for the same handler. The mid-response byte drop is an accepted deviation; this log-and-side-effect on a clean hijack is not.
- [minor] Handler sets `w.Header()["ETag"] = []string{""}` (non-canonical key). `h.Get`/`h.Set` use the canonical "Etag", so the wire carries two ETag lines: `""` and the computed tag. Not reproduced in a real handler using `Header().Set`.
- [minor] Plain net/http logs "superfluous response.WriteHeader call" for a second WriteHeader; the wrapper swallows it silently. Behavior of the status is the same; only logging differs.
- [minor] `FEATURE_FLOW.md` is an untracked file in the workspace that is not part of the criteria or the README change. Confirm whether it belongs in the change or should be removed.
- [minor] Doc comment says buffering is "in memory" but the flush-commit description is fine; no other doc sentence mismatch found.
=== IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 1 (sent after review 1) ===
GOAL: Fix one reviewer finding in middleware/etag.go (repo /tmp/ff-eval-o8lsryxp/workspace, go-chi/chi v5).

FINDING [blocking]: When a GET/HEAD handler hijacks the connection via `etagResponseWriter.Hijack` (directly or via http.NewResponseController), `finish()` still runs after the handler returns and calls `startStreaming` -> `ResponseWriter.WriteHeader`, so net/http logs `http: response.WriteHeader on hijacked connection` on every hijacked request. Plain net/http logs nothing. Fix: when Hijack succeeds, mark the writer hijacked, and make `finish()` do nothing for a hijacked writer. Add a test in middleware/etag_test.go with a real httptest.NewServer that hijacks, writes a raw HTTP response, and asserts the client gets it AND that the server's ErrorLog (set `ts.Config.ErrorLog = log.New(&buf, "", 0)` via httptest.NewUnstartedServer) stays empty. Keep the change minimal; don't change other behavior (304 keeps deleting Last-Modified as net/http does — that's intended).

FILES: middleware/etag.go, middleware/etag_test.go.
CONSTRAINTS: touch nothing else.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. `middleware.ETag(next http.Handler) http.Handler` exists in `middleware/etag.go` with a doc comment (says it buffers whole GET/HEAD responses in memory, so it is unsuited to large or streamed responses, and that If-None-Match uses weak comparison). Tests live in `middleware/etag_test.go`. No new dependencies.
2. GET and HEAD: the response is buffered. If the final status is 200 (explicit `WriteHeader(200)` or implicit via first `Write`, or no write at all) and the handler did not set an `ETag` header, the middleware sets `ETag` to a strong entity tag computed from the buffered body: double-quoted, no `W/` prefix, only hex chars inside the quotes (e.g. `"` + hex of a sha256/truncated hash + `"`). Same body -> same tag; different body -> different tag; empty body still gets a tag. The body and all other headers the handler set are delivered unchanged.
   - Hostile: handler writes nothing at all; handler writes in many small chunks (tag equals the tag of the concatenated body); body of several MB.
3. A handler-set `ETag` (strong or weak, e.g. `W/"v1"`) is never overwritten or altered.
4. If-None-Match: for a 200 GET/HEAD response, if any member of the request's If-None-Match matches the response ETag under RFC 9110 weak comparison (opaque-tags equal, `W/` ignored on either side), or the field value is `*`, respond `304 Not Modified` with an empty body instead. The 304 keeps the `ETag` header and other headers (Cache-Control, Vary, Date, Expires, Content-Location), and drops `Content-Type`, `Content-Length` and `Content-Encoding` (as net/http's ServeContent does). All If-None-Match header lines are considered (`r.Header.Values`). Comma-separated lists with optional whitespace (`"a" , W/"b",  "c"`) are parsed.
   - Hostile: `W/"x"` request vs strong `"x"` response and vice versa -> 304; `"x"` vs `"xy"` or `"X"` -> 200 (no prefix/case match); empty or whitespace-only If-None-Match -> 200; malformed members (unquoted `abc`, unterminated `"abc`, `W/abc`, stray commas `,,`) never produce a match and never panic — follow net/http's checkIfNoneMatch behavior (skip empty members, stop at a malformed one); `*` mixed into a list is not special unless it is the whole value; a handler-set unquoted (malformed) ETag `abc` does not match request `"abc"`.
5. Other methods (POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, OPTIONS, ...) pass through unchanged: the handler gets the original ResponseWriter, nothing is buffered, no ETag is added, and If-None-Match is ignored (no 304).
6. Non-200 final statuses (201, 204, 206, 301, 404, 500, ...) on GET/HEAD pass through unchanged: same status, headers and body, no ETag added, no 304 even if If-None-Match is `*` or matches a handler-set ETag. 1xx informational WriteHeader calls (e.g. 103) are forwarded immediately and do not fix the final status. A second WriteHeader call is ignored, like net/http.
7. The wrapping writer forwards optional capabilities like `compressResponseWriter` in middleware/compress.go: `Flush` (calling it stops buffering: commits the status and headers as they stand — no computed ETag, no 304 — writes the buffered bytes, flushes the underlying writer if it can, and later writes stream straight through), `Hijack` and `Push` (forwarded, or return a `chi/middleware: ...` error when the underlying writer lacks them), and `Unwrap() http.ResponseWriter` so `http.NewResponseController` works.
8. HEAD: same ETag and 304 behavior as GET; the tag for HEAD is computed from whatever the handler wrote (net/http discards a HEAD body itself).
9. No shared mutable state between requests; tests pass under `-race`, including a test that serves concurrent requests.
10. README "Core middlewares" table gets an `[ETag]` row (placed alphabetically between ContentCharset/CleanPath and GetHead) and the link `[ETag]: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware#ETag` in the link list below, in matching position. No other README lines change; CHANGELOG.md untouched.
11. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...` pass and `gofmt -l .` prints nothing. Existing tests still pass.

CHECKS: while working `go test -race ./middleware -run ETag`; at the end `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .`.
